title: Paloma Security Card: Sign-In Lock Settings of the Personal Sender Account Levels
content:
Paloma Security sets four sign-in lock settings on the Personal Sender Account for each verification level: how many consecutive failed sign-ins lock the account, after how many minutes a failed-sign-in lock releases itself without contact, which lock reasons a support agent may release once the caller has passed identity verification, and whether an agent release also needs an accepted, unexpired government ID on file.

| Level | Consecutive failed sign-ins that lock the account | Self-release of a failed-sign-in lock (minutes) | Lock reasons a support agent may release | Accepted, unexpired government ID on file needed for an agent release |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paloma Starter | 5 | 30 | failed sign-ins; password-reset abuse; device-change review | no |
| Paloma Verified | 5 | 30 | failed sign-ins; password-reset abuse; device-change review | no |
| Paloma Verified Plus | 5 | 30 | failed sign-ins; password-reset abuse; device-change review | yes |
| Paloma Enhanced | 5 | 60 | failed sign-ins; password-reset abuse; device-change review | yes |
| Paloma Premier | 4 | 0 | failed sign-ins; password-reset abuse | yes |
| Paloma Private Client | 4 | 0 | failed sign-ins; password-reset abuse | yes |

A self-release figure of 0 minutes means the lock never releases itself.

## Points of reading

- A lock for suspected account takeover is not in the agent-releasable list at any level.
- At Paloma Premier and Paloma Private Client a lock placed for a device-change review is not agent-releasable either, and a failed-sign-in lock never releases itself.
- From Paloma Verified Plus upward an agent release also needs the government ID condition in the last column.
